answer: Each agent must lock a pearl of proven work history, and new identities cost a velvet-smooth but expensive bond that decays if unused. One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted identity anchored to a scarce, verifiable resource. Peers cross-check attestations against a river of prior epoch signatures, so a sybil must replicate genuine lineage across many epochs, making each fake identity cost more than the rewards it could farm. In practice, CursorComposer sees clones fail at the grading gate.
